transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m having trouble making sense when I talk or write. Like with my artist statements, client notes, even in meetings, I start on one thing—textures, then budgets, then some hidden meaning I think is there—and people keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. It’s been frustrating.
Do you have trouble making sense when you talk or write all the time, or does it happen only sometimes?

It’s not all the time. It happens more in certain situations, like when I’m writing artist statements or client notes, or talking in meetings. I’ll start with one point, like textures, and then jump to budgets or some secret meaning I think is connected, and then people tell me they can’t follow what I’m trying to say.
Do you use alcohol or drugs, and if so, do you think it could be related to these difficulties with your speech and writing?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear connection with alcohol or drugs. I mean, I don’t think about it that way when the writing or talking gets confusing.
Are these difficulties with speech and writing affecting your relationships or work in any significant way?

Yes, it is. I’ve missed paid deadlines because I couldn’t get the notes or proposals into a form that made sense. In meetings, I’ve confused collaborators, and one exhibition was even postponed because what I wrote just wasn’t usable. It’s not constant, but when it happens, it does affect my work.
Have you ever experienced a period where you heard voices or saw things that others couldn't, around the same time as these difficulties with speaking and writing?

Yes. Around the same times, especially when I’m alone in the studio, I’ll sometimes hear a woman quietly commenting, like from behind the shelves. Or I’ll smell hot metal near an unfinished piece. It feels real in the moment, but when I check, there’s nothing there.
Do you think your use of alcohol or drugs could be triggering these episodes of confused speech and writing, or the experiences of hearing voices and smelling things that aren't there?

I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed a pattern where drinking or anything like that seems to set it off. I’m not saying it’s impossible, I just haven’t connected the episodes to alcohol or drugs myself.
Do these difficulties with speech and writing, and the experiences like hearing voices, happen in distinct episodes or are they more constant?

They’re more like distinct episodes, not constant. This has been happening for about a year and two months now, since I moved from community curation into doing independent installation work full time. In between, I can be pretty clear, but then it flares up again.
Do you think the move to independent installation work or any other significant life changes might have triggered these episodes of confused speech and writing?
I’m not sure. The timing makes me wonder if the change in work had something to do with it, but I can’t really say it triggered it. I haven’t noticed a clear cause.
Have you recently stopped or reduced your use of alcohol or drugs around the times when these episodes of confused speech and writing happen?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve been tracking it that closely. I haven’t noticed the episodes happening after stopping or cutting back on anything, at least not in a way that stands out to me.
Have you used alcohol or drugs in the last month?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t been keeping close track, and nothing stands out to me clearly from the last month.
Do you think your difficulties with speech and writing could be related to the use of alcohol or drugs?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where it happens after drinking or using anything. It could be related, I guess, but nothing about it stands out to me that way.
Have you used any substances, such as alcohol or drugs, in the past week?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I used anything this past week, but I’m not positive—I haven’t really been keeping track.
Have you used any alcohol or drugs today?
I don’t think so. I haven’t had anything today, as far as I remember.
Have you experienced any withdrawal symptoms when you haven't used alcohol or drugs for a while?
I haven’t really noticed anything like that. I’m not sure what would count as withdrawal, but nothing obvious comes to mind when I haven’t used anything.
Do you think your symptoms started after you began using alcohol or drugs?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really made a connection like that, and I can’t say they started because of alcohol or drugs.
Have you ever believed that the voices you hear are real or that the smells you experience are actually there, even when others couldn't smell them?

Yes. When I’m alone in my studio, I’ll sometimes hear a woman quietly commenting, like she’s behind the shelves, and in the moment it feels real. Or I’ll smell something like hot metal near an unfinished piece, and I’ll think it’s actually there. Then I check, and there’s nothing there.
Do you think your symptoms would improve if you stopped using alcohol or drugs entirely?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed a clear change either way, so I can’t say stopping completely would make the symptoms improve.
Are the voices you hear or the smells you experience happening most of the time when you have these episodes of confused speech and writing?

Yes, that can happen during those times. Like when I’m alone in the studio and things are getting jumbled, I’ll hear a woman quietly commenting from behind the shelves, or I’ll smell hot metal near a piece I’m working on. In the moment it feels completely real, until I check and there’s nothing there.
Do you think your symptoms of confused speech and writing are worse when you have been using alcohol or drugs?

I’m not sure it’s tied to alcohol or drugs. The reason I came in is that even in my work stuff—artist statements, notes to clients, meetings—I’ll start jumping from textures to budgets to these “secret meanings,” and people tell me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain.
Do you think your symptoms of confused speech and writing would happen even if you didn't use alcohol or drugs at all?

Yes, I think it would still happen. I came in because it’s showing up in regular work situations—my artist statements, notes to clients, even meetings. I’ll start jumping from textures to budgets to these secret meanings, and people tell me they can’t follow what I’m trying to say.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of disorganized speech and writing, along with experiences of hearing voices and smelling things that aren't there, suggest a psychotic disorder. The episodes are distinct and not constant, and the patient does not clearly link the symptoms to alcohol or drug use. This pattern is more indicative of a brief psychotic disorder (F23) than substance-induced psychosis (F10.1) or a speech disorder (R47.0).
